decisions.reason: Probe lines 59-70 and 92-130 state Define-XML ADTTE.ADT as written: the guide page-5 AOCC01FL occurrence supplies ADT only when its ASTDT is nonmissing and strictly after TRTSDT, else the converted ADSL.RFENDTC. In each of the five differing records the reference ADT is that selected ASTDT on TRTSDT itself, a same-day event that only the inclusive ADAE.TRTEMFL and SAP page-16 boundary admits, so the pattern follows from the strict literal rule.

Define-XML ADTTE.STARTDT names ADSL.RFSTDTC (DM.RFSTDTC in the ADSL.RFSTDTC section), but adtte_v1.yaml line 166 reads ADSL.TRTSDT, which Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT documents from SV.SVSTDTC and the ADSL specification derives from MIN(EX.EXSTDTC). The specification never routes STARTDT through RFSTDTC, so agreement of the observed dates does not make TRTSDT the documented copy source.

Define-XML ADTTE.ADT requires a nonmissing ADAE.ASTDT strictly after TRTSDT, but adtte_v1.yaml lines 181-184 branch only on HAS_EVENT, which lines 168-175 set from FIRST_DERM.AESEQ presence after the AOCC01FL filter at lines 63-75. That flag rests on the inclusive Define-XML ADAE.TRTEMFL test ASTDT >= TRTSDT, so nothing on this path imposes the strict date guard.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCSEQ requires AESEQ when SRCDOM=ADAE and null otherwise; adtte_v1.yaml lines 168-175 and 215-222 set SRCDOM to ADAE exactly when FIRST_DERM.AESEQ is nonmissing. The direct FIRST_DERM.AESEQ read at line 236 therefore states both branches by construction, a paraphrase rather than a different clause.

The guide page-5 and Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL state chronological ASTDT/AESEQ ordering, but no retained section specifies placement of missing sort keys. FIRST_DERM in adtte.yaml lines 71-73 adds nulls: last for both keys on the ADT source path.

Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL and the guide page-5 describe ASTDT/AESEQ order but do not state a missing-key ordering rule anywhere in the retained sections. The CNSR path uses FIRST_DERM through HAS_EVENT, including the explicit nulls: last choices at adtte.yaml lines 71-73.

The guide page-5 and Define-XML ADAE.AOCC01FL document the source occurrence and ASTDT/AESEQ ordering without defining where missing keys sort. SRCSEQ reads FIRST_DERM.AESEQ, whose helper adds the undocumented nulls: last choices at adtte.yaml lines 71-73.

SAP page-10 defines end of study among general data handling conventions and states no ADT censoring date or visit-to-RFENDTC mapping, and no retained section ties ADTTE censoring to that definition. Define-XML ADTTE.ADT names the RFENDTC conversion, which adtte_v1.yaml line 184 supplies through ADSL.RFENDT (Define-XML ADSL.RFENDT: RFENDTC converted to SAS date), so no documented ADT clause is missing.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCDOM defines the domain only as the source used to populate ADT, and neither that section nor the guide page-5 states a precedence when the flagged ADAE.ASTDT and ADSL.RFENDT both equal the published ADT. The strict Define-XML ADTTE.ADT condition cannot settle it because it does not reproduce published ADT (ADTTE.ADT.CR-5), and retired probe lines 147-153 rederive that condition rather than state a claimed literal.

Define-XML ADTTE.SRCVAR defines the variable only as the source used to populate ADT; ADSL.RFENDT identifies RFENDT as the converted RFENDTC fallback, but no retained section states which variable applies when the flagged ADAE.ASTDT and ADSL.RFENDT both equal published ADT. The strict ADTTE.ADT condition does not reproduce published ADT (ADTTE.ADT.CR-5), so retired probe lines 154-160, which rederive it, are not an independent literal and the gap stands.
